## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode goal prompt cache preservation - NEW MEDIUM PRIORITY (command)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #14680 "fix(goal): preserve prompt cache across goal turns and keep timers running" merged 2026-09-30 ~09:00 UTC. Keeps goal tool schemas stable so starting, continuing, and finishing a goal does not invalidate the provider prompt cache. Tool schemas generated once at goal start and reused across all turns (schema regeneration on each turn was invalidating cache because schema order/content could vary). Carries the user's shell and custom system context into automatic goal turns, including after compaction, and refreshes it from real user input instead of rescanning the growing transcript (avoids costly context recompute per turn). Keeps the session working timer running across goal turns and between-turn waits instead of resetting each turn. Rejected commands no longer clear an active goal's clock; completion, pause, blocking, and terminal errors still stop it. Commit sha `e1f3a8d` (merge commit), real commits in PR (fix goal prompt cache, fix vscode hold goal timer through transient offline).

- **Why**: **Alexi HAS a goal command** (`src/command/goal.ts` 263 lines, autonomous loop using `agenticChat()` to work toward a condition, evaluates condition via LLM after each iteration, supports progress tracking / cancellation / max turns safety cap / event bus progress emission). Subagent search confirmed "Goal Tool ✅ EXISTS" as a command/feature (not a registered tool). However, Alexi goal command does NOT preserve tool schemas across goal iterations — each call to `agenticChat()` inside the goal loop (`goal.ts` L144-176 loop body) may regenerate tool schemas dynamically, and if schema order/content varies (e.g. due to tool registry changes, conditional tool availability, or provider-specific schema generation), the prompt cache breakpoint is invalidated and the full prompt is resent. Current `goal.ts` does not cache tool schemas at goal start or pass a frozen schema list through the loop. **Alexi also does NOT have a working timer feature** — subagent search confirmed "Timer/Working-Time Tracking Features ⚠️ LIMITED" with only session-level duration tracking (`metadata.updated - metadata.created` in `src/core/sessionManager.ts`) and goal-specific elapsed time (`elapsedMs` in goal loop). No dedicated timer tool for starting/stopping/pausing work timers, so Kilocode's "keep timers running across goal turns" fix does not directly apply (we don't have timers to keep running). Cache preservation IS relevant and HIGH IMPACT (goal loops with many turns waste tokens/cost/latency by invalidating cache on each turn). MEDIUM PRIORITY ~4-6h (cache tool schemas at goal start, pass frozen schemas to all `agenticChat()` calls inside goal loop, verify prompt cache hit rate across turns in tests, add test case for goal loop with 5+ turns checking cache metrics).

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14680 (Kilocode goal prompt cache preservation, merged 2026-09-30 ~09:00 UTC), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/command/goal.ts L1-263 (goal command implementation, agenticChat loop L144-176), subagent search finding "Goal Tool ✅ EXISTS as a command/feature" and "Timer/Working-Time Tracking Features ⚠️ LIMITED (session duration only, no dedicated timer tool)"

- **Category**: command (goal loop optimization, prompt cache preservation)

- **Size**: MEDIUM ~4-6h (cache tool schemas at goal start before loop, pass frozen schemas to all `agenticChat()` calls in goal loop via options/context, verify prompt cache hit rate improves across goal turns in integration test, add test case for goal loop with 5+ turns checking `cache_read_input_tokens` increases after turn 1, verify `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test` green)

#### 2. Cline Linux TUI glyph compatibility - NEW LOW PRIORITY (cli)

- **What**: Cline PR #14686 "fix(cli): use widely supported glyph for auto-approve status indicator" merged 2026-09-30 ~08:00 UTC. Swaps U+23F5 (BLACK MEDIUM RIGHT-POINTING TRIANGLE) to U+25B6 (BLACK RIGHT-POINTING TRIANGLE) for auto-approve status indicator. U+23F5 is missing from nearly all Linux monospace fonts (DejaVu Sans Mono, JetBrains Mono, Cascadia, Noto Sans Mono, etc.) so indicator rendered as tofu (empty box) or nothing. U+25B6 is already used elsewhere in the TUI and is present in common Linux fonts. Keeps U+23F5 on macOS/Windows where system fallback fonts cover it (platform-specific glyph selection). Commit sha `4b2c3e5`.

- **Why**: **Alexi TUI** (`src/cli/tui/` and `src/cli/interactive.tsx`) uses various Unicode glyphs for UI elements: spinners (`src/cli/tui/dialogs/SessionList.tsx`, ink-spinner package), status indicators (likely in chat display, approval prompts, progress bars), borders (Ink Box component default chars), but **has NOT been audited for Linux monospace font coverage**. Glyphs missing from DejaVu Sans Mono (most common Linux terminal font) or JetBrains Mono (popular dev font) will render as tofu (U+FFFD replacement character or empty box), degrading UX. Current TUI code does not have platform-specific glyph fallbacks (no `process.platform === 'linux'` checks for glyph selection). Subagent search confirmed "Browser Tool ✅ EXISTS" with full Puppeteer integration (`src/tool/tools/browser.ts` 492 lines), so TUI glyphs are likely present in output formatting. LOW PRIORITY ~2-3h (audit TUI code for Unicode glyphs outside ASCII/Latin-1 range, identify glyphs missing from DejaVu Sans Mono / JetBrains Mono via font coverage check, replace with widely supported alternatives or add platform-specific fallbacks for Linux, test on Linux VM with common terminal fonts).

- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14686 (Cline Linux TUI glyph compatibility, merged 2026-09-30 ~08:00 UTC), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/cli/tui/ (TUI components), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/cli/interactive.tsx (interactive REPL), subagent search finding "Browser Tool ✅ EXISTS" (TUI output formatting likely uses glyphs)

- **Category**: cli (TUI glyph font compatibility, Linux UX)

- **Size**: SMALL ~2-3h (audit TUI code under `src/cli/tui/` and `src/cli/interactive.tsx` for Unicode glyphs outside ASCII range U+0020-U+007E, check glyph coverage in DejaVu Sans Mono and JetBrains Mono via Unicode font charts or test rendering, replace missing glyphs with widely supported alternatives from U+2500-U+257F Box Drawing / U+25A0-U+25FF Geometric Shapes, add platform-specific fallback via `process.platform === 'linux' ? FALLBACK_GLYPH : PREFERRED_GLYPH` pattern, test on Linux VM with DejaVu Sans Mono, verify `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test` green)
